name: Poke
tagline: An AI assistant that lives in your text messages
description: Poke is a personal assistant you text in Messages, WhatsApp or Telegram, connected to your email, calendar and apps. GAIA works from the same chat apps and adds web and desktop apps, workflows across your tools and source-available code.
metaTitle: Poke AI Alternatives: GAIA vs Poke, Side by Side
metaDescription: Poke lives in your texts. GAIA works in iMessage, WhatsApp and Telegram too, and adds web and desktop apps, triggered workflows and source-available code.
intro: Poke made a good idea popular: an assistant you simply text, with no app to learn. It connects to your email and calendar, nudges you when something needs attention, and runs recipes from the chat. GAIA shares the messaging habit, working in iMessage, WhatsApp and Telegram, and goes past the chat window: a web and desktop app for longer work, workflows triggered by your tools, memory you can inspect, and code that is public under a source-available license.

rows.gaia: A personal AI assistant you reach from chat apps, the web and the desktop, working across email, calendar, tasks and your other tools
rows.competitor: A text-based assistant from The Interaction Company, acquired by Cognition in July 2026; you reach it in Messages, WhatsApp and Telegram

rows.gaia: Workflows that run on a schedule or when something happens in Gmail, Google Calendar, Slack, GitHub, Linear and more
rows.competitor: Proactive nudges from connected email, calendar and apps; background automations on its paid plan

rows.gaia: Gmail, Outlook, Google Calendar, Slack, Notion, GitHub, Linear, Todoist, Asana, HubSpot and more, plus custom MCP servers
rows.competitor: Gmail, Google Calendar, Outlook, Notion, Linear, GitHub and more, plus custom integrations through MCP and shareable recipes

rows.gaia: Long-term memory of your preferences and people that you can view, edit and delete in settings
rows.competitor: Uses memory of past chats; what it stores and how you edit it is not documented publicly

rows.gaia: Source-available (PolyForm Noncommercial) with self-hosting via Docker
Multi-step workflows with schedule and integration triggers, editable in the app
rows.competitor: Recipes and plain-English automations, set up and run inside the chat

rows.gaia: iMessage, WhatsApp, Telegram, Slack and Discord, plus a web app and a desktop app for macOS, Windows and Linux
rows.competitor: No app to install; everything happens in Messages, WhatsApp or Telegram

gaiaAdvantages: The same texting habit, plus web and desktop apps for longer work
Workflows triggered by your email, calendar and team tools
Memory you can see, edit and delete
A desktop app that can look at your screen and use your clipboard
competitorAdvantages: Nothing to install: it lives entirely in your text messages
Approved as the first AI agent on Apple's Messages for Business
A community library of shareable recipes
verdict: Choose Poke if you want an assistant that lives only in your texts and you like building with recipes. Choose GAIA if you want the same chat convenience plus a web and desktop app, workflows that run across your tools, memory you control and code you can inspect.

faqs.question: What makes GAIA different from Poke?
faqs.answer: Both are assistants you can text. Poke lives only inside your messaging apps. GAIA also has a web app and a desktop app, runs workflows triggered by your tools, lets you view and edit everything it remembers, and is source-available under the PolyForm Noncommercial license.

faqs.question: Does GAIA work in iMessage like Poke?
faqs.answer: Yes. You link iMessage in GAIA's settings with your phone number and then text GAIA in Messages. It also works in WhatsApp, Telegram, Slack and Discord.

faqs.question: Is there a source-available alternative to Poke?
faqs.answer: GAIA is one. Its code is public under the PolyForm Noncommercial license, so you can read it and self-host it for personal, noncommercial use. The hosted service is a paid subscription.
